title: Climate Risk Profile: Iraq
methodology: PIK/ISIMIP-linked multi-model projections under RCP2.6/RCP6.0; sectoral impact modeling
limitations: Precipitation/water projections less certain; socioeconomic change not incorporated in climate-model impacts. (Weathering Risk)

title: Nationally Determined Contribution, Updated in 2025
methodology: Government policy, sectoral planning, institutional arrangements and targets
limitations: Commitments and targets demonstrate intended policy/capacity, not evaluated outcomes.

title: Second National Communication and First Biennial Update Report
geographic_coverage: National plus governorate and Southern Mesopotamian analyses
methodology: ERA5/ECMWF, TerraClimate, NEX-GDDP 21-GCM ensemble, CORDEX, APSIM, sector/stakeholder assessment
limitations: Some underlying strategic studies are older; local crop resolution explicitly limited; RCP framework rather than newer SSPs.

title: Iraq Country Climate and Development Report
methodology: Integrated macro, sector, energy, water/agriculture and distributional analysis
limitations: Publication page and report link verified; detailed claims in this packet are assigned to the accessible Economic Monitor synopsis where exact PDF locators were checked. (World Bank)

title: Iraq Economic Monitor: A New Opportunity to Reform
methodology: Macroeconomic analysis and special-focus synthesis of CCDR modeling
limitations: Climate economic estimates are modelled scenarios, not observed causal effects. (World Bank)

title: Country Partnership Framework for Iraq FY2022-FY2026
methodology: Country diagnostics, portfolio experience and strategic programming
limitations: Predates the most recent water crisis and NDC; program intentions are not evidence of outcomes. (World Bank)

title: Tigris Adaptation and Healthy River Project - Concept-stage PID
limitations: Concept-stage project; proposed financing and activities must not be treated as achieved results.

title: Advocacy Note: Water Scarcity and Climate Risks in Iraq
methodology: Synthesis of water, displacement and humanitarian indicators
limitations: Advocacy document rather than independent causal study; some underlying datasets are summarized rather than reproduced. (The United Nations in Iraq)

title: Localised interlinkages between climate, peace, and security in Iraq
geographic_coverage: National synthesis plus selected local cases
methodology: 15 semi-structured interviews, 46 internal reports/case studies, media/analytical sources; UN Climate Security Mechanism framework
limitations: Qualitative and purposive; selected cases explicitly not exhaustive; some supporting sources are secondary.

title: Climate, Peace and Security Fact Sheet: Iraq
limitations: Secondary synthesis; many pathway claims rely on prior literature rather than causal identification. (SIPRI)

title: Climate change effects on conflict dynamics in Iraq: Makhmur, Tal Afar and Al-Rifai
methodology: 20 in-depth interviews and 10 focus groups with 124 participants, plus contextual analysis
limitations: Three purposively selected districts; women underrepresented in IDIs; perception evidence cannot establish national causality. (Berghof Foundation)

title: Local Climate Change Adaptation Plan for Kurdistan Region - Iraq
temporal_coverage: Historical baseline and future scenarios; plan current from 2024
methodology: Participatory technical working group, climate vulnerability assessment, sector adaptation planning
limitations: KRI-specific; proposed interventions/MRL are planned capacity rather than demonstrated outcomes.

title: Independent Country Programme Evaluation: Iraq
geographic_coverage: North, central and south; national programme
methodology: UNEG-standard evaluation; triangulation; 215 stakeholder interviews; field visits; GIS analysis
limitations: Security/visa constraints cancelled planned visits to Kirkuk, Sulaymaniyah and Najaf; some projects unfinished.

title: Evaluation of Iraq WFP Country Strategic Plan 2020-2024
methodology: Independent strategic/portfolio evaluation of relevance, effectiveness, efficiency and performance
limitations: Full report download was not accessible through the browsing environment; official page conclusions were accessible. Page displays “3 May 2023” despite evaluation coverage extending to Oct 2023, so publication-date metadata requires independent confirmation. (World Food Programme)

title: GCF approves USD 39 million for SRVALI project
organization: FAO / GCF / United Nations in Iraq
methodology: Programme design, financing and intended beneficiary/outcome statements
limitations: Announcement only; beneficiary numbers and expected effects are targets, not evaluated performance. (The United Nations in Iraq)
